reason: Sunlight can evaporate seawater, starting the journey back to shore as fresh water.
expectation: Water will evaporate from the sea, leaving dissolved salts behind.

effect: Evaporation provides water vapor for the return journey while dissolved minerals largely remain in the sea.
reaction: Satisfying to see the water cycle begin from the existing sea.
reason: Cooler air should help the evaporated water condense into clouds.

choice.with: Cooler air high above the surface

expectation: The water vapor will condense into droplets or clouds.

effect: The evaporated seawater has condensed into a cloud, ready to be transported toward shore.
reaction: The separation of water from dissolved minerals makes the fresh-water route clear.
reason: Wind should carry the cloud inland toward the rocky rise, so I will first try moving it with the wind.
expectation: The wind will carry the cloud toward the coast.

effect: The cloud has moved over land, setting up rainfall near the shore.
reaction: The wind connects evaporation at sea with rainfall elsewhere.
reason: The rocky rise may lift the cloud and encourage cooling and rain.

choice.with: A rocky rise behind the shore

expectation: Air rising over the rock will cool, helping the cloud produce rain.

effect: Rain has fallen on the rise and can now flow back toward the shore.
reaction: The rise provides a clear link between cloud movement and rainfall.
reason: The slope should carry rainwater downhill toward the basin and shore.

choice.with: A slope toward a broad basin

expectation: Fresh water will flow down the slope toward the shore.

effect: The stream completes the fresh-water return goal; moonlight remains to be placed on water.
reaction: The completed water cycle is satisfying.
reason: Sunlight reflected by the Moon should provide the moonlight needed for the remaining goal.

choice.with: The Moon with a pale early crust

expectation: The Moon will reflect sunlight as moonlight.

effect: Reflected sunlight is now available for the remaining moonlight goal.
reaction: The distinction between reflected light and the Moon’s formation heat is useful.
reason: A tidal pool offers a surface for the reflected moonlight.

choice.with: Pools left behind by the tide

expectation: Moonlight will appear in the sheltered pools.

effect: Reflected sunlight cannot currently be combined directly with the tidal pools, so another preparation is needed.
reason: A cooling night may prepare the setting for moonlight; inspection will show its available partners.

choice.inspect: A cooling night above the coast

expectation: The inspection will reveal how the night contributes to the moonlight scene.

effect: The night and tidal pools made a still pool, preparing the remaining moonlight scene.
reaction: The automatic preparation clarified why the earlier pairing failed.
reason: The Moon may now illuminate the prepared still pool.

choice.combine: The Moon with a pale early crust

expectation: Moonlight will appear reflected in the still pool.

effect: The Moon itself cannot currently be combined with the still pool; the reflected sunlight may now be usable instead.
reaction: Another failed pairing is a little frustrating, but it suggests trying the prepared light.
reason: The still pool is now prepared to receive the previously created reflected sunlight.
expectation: Moonlight will appear in the still pool.

effect: The reflected sunlight and still pool completed the moonlight goal and the chapter.
reaction: The quiet rock-pool reflection was a satisfying finish after the failed pairings.

mostWorthwhile.text: Returning seawater to shore as rain and a stream was worthwhile: the sequence clearly connected evaporation, transport, rainfall and runoff.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two failed moonlight pairings interrupted the ending; it was not clear initially that the pool needed a separate night-time preparation.

surprise.text: I was surprised that reflected sunlight could not be combined with the tidal pools until night prepared them as a still pool.

arbitrary.text: Requiring a still pool is understandable, but making the Moon itself incompatible with it felt somewhat arbitrary once the scene was prepared.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the water-cycle sequence made familiar processes feel connected, and the quiet final scene provided a rewarding destination.
